method: Fresh seven-shot anonymous A/B review from an isolated headless browser. Quality was chosen before opening each randomized side map; identity was revealed afterward. The canonical terrestrial winter reference is sr_13.jpg.

shots.gap: The road and car read clearly, but ours has sparse card-like grass, species-incoherent tree silhouettes, and hard planar verge patches. The bar has continuous rolling landform, denser grounded foliage, and stronger near/mid/far depth.
Ours has pale gray-green shoulders, flat tuft scatter, and weak contact/shadow structure. The bar carries warm amber fields, long shadows, and a more finished dusk exposure.
Ours has stars and a readable road but most terrain collapses into blue-black low-poly silhouettes and the headlight field is weak. The bar preserves landform, road response, and nocturnal depth.

shots.gap: Ours is a coherent terrestrial winter road, but retains sparse dark trunks/cards, hard snow-road shoulder seams, and a clear blue horizon. The bar has layered snowy relief, falling snow, and continuous guardrail/road contact.

shots.gap: Ours has an elevated road but the inland valley is flattened by repeated dark cards and lacks water/ridge separation. The bar has cut/fill terrain, shoreline context, and clear aerial layering.

shots.gap: The wheel and centered road are legible, but ours has a noisy faceted dashboard, repeated silhouettes, and planar verge artifacts. The bar has cleaner cockpit framing, guardrail, lane treatment, and grounded roadside materials.

regression_check.evidence: Current tree and shrub instances remain in stable vertical frames rather than inheriting terrain tilt; no new broad crown-banking regression is visible in the seven r41 captures.
regression_check.residual: The dominant low-poly grass/terrain-card and material-depth gap remains, so removing that regression does not change the quality winner.

max_gap: Continuous grounded landscape integration remains the largest mismatch: stamped foliage and hard-edged verge planes flatten near/mid/far material depth across every camera. Secondary gaps are golden/night material response, missing vista water/ridge context, cockpit occlusion, and winter atmosphere/contact.
notes: All seven captures completed at 1920x1080 with full residency and no page errors.
Quality calls were made from anonymous A/B images before opening the side maps; all seven identity guesses were correct.
